subject: maths
chapter_title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

concepts.title: Formulation of Linear Equations in Two Variables
concepts.definition: Formulating two linear relationships between two unknown variables to model word problems in standard algebraic representation.
concepts.key_idea: Convert real-world constraints into a pair of simultaneous linear equations.
question_patterns: form pair of linear equations from the given word problem
represent the given situation algebraically using two variables
write linear equations in two variables for the given statement
translate the word problem into a system of two linear equations
express the given real life situation as linear equations

solution_steps.action: Assign variables to unknown quantities
solution_steps.explain: Define variable x for the first unknown quantity and y for the second unknown quantity.

solution_steps.action: Formulate equations from given conditions
solution_steps.explain: Translate each statement into an algebraic linear equation relating x and y.

solution_steps.action: Verify the pair of equations captures all constraints
solution_steps.explain: Check that both equations together represent every condition stated in the word problem.

concepts.title: Consistency and Graphical Behavior via Coefficient Ratios
concepts.definition: Comparing ratios of corresponding coefficients of x, y, and constant terms to determine line behavior and number of solutions.
concepts.formula: a1/a2 != b1/b2 (unique solution); a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2 (infinitely many); a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2 (no solution)
concepts.key_idea: Coefficient ratios reveal if lines intersect uniquely, run parallel with no solution, or coincide infinitely.
question_patterns: compare ratios a1/a2, b1/b2, c1/c2 to check consistency
find whether lines are intersecting, parallel or coincident
determine if the pair of linear equations is consistent or inconsistent
check if the system of equations has unique, infinitely many, or no solutions
examine the ratio of coefficients to classify the pair of lines

solution_steps.action: Identify coefficients a1, b1, c1 and a2, b2, c2
solution_steps.explain: Write both equations in standard form a*x + b*y + c = 0 to read coefficients.

solution_steps.action: Compute and compare ratios a1/a2, b1/b2, and c1/c2
solution_steps.explain: If a1/a2 != b1/b2, lines intersect uniquely (consistent). If a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2, lines coincide (dependent consistent). If a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2, lines are parallel (inconsistent).

solution_steps.action: Classify the system as consistent or inconsistent
solution_steps.explain: Conclude whether the pair has a unique solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solution based on the ratio comparison.

concepts.title: Graphical Solution of a Pair of Linear Equations
concepts.definition: Finding common solution values of two linear equations by drawing their graphs on a coordinate grid and locating the point of intersection.
concepts.formula: point (x, y) where line 1 intersects line 2
concepts.key_idea: Graph intersection coordinates represent the simultaneous solution to both linear equations.
question_patterns: solve the pair of linear equations graphically
find the solution of linear equations by plotting graph
determine coordinates of intersection point of two lines graphically
graph the linear equations and find their common point
check graphically if the given pair of equations has a solution

solution_steps.action: Obtain solution tables for both linear equations
solution_steps.explain: Find at least two (x, y) coordinate pairs for each line.

solution_steps.action: Plot the lines on graph paper and find intersection
solution_steps.explain: Draw straight lines through the plotted points and identify coordinate (x, y) where they intersect.

solution_steps.action: Verify the intersection point satisfies both equations
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the intersection coordinates back into both original equations to confirm they hold true.

concepts.title: Substitution Method for Solving Linear Equations
concepts.definition: Solving simultaneous linear equations by isolating one variable from one equation and substituting its expression into the second equation.
concepts.formula: x = (c1 - b1*y)/a1 substituted into a2*x + b2*y + c2 = 0
concepts.key_idea: Express one variable in terms of the other to reduce two equations to a single variable linear equation.
question_patterns: solve the pair of linear equations by substitution method
use substitution to find the values of x and y
find the solution of the system using algebraic substitution
apply substitution method to solve the equations
determine x and y by expressing one variable in terms of another

solution_steps.action: Express one variable in terms of the other from one equation
solution_steps.explain: Isolate variable x or y in the convenient linear equation.

solution_steps.action: Substitute this expression into the other equation
solution_steps.explain: Replace the isolated variable in the second equation to get an equation in one variable.

solution_steps.action: Solve for the single variable and back-substitute
solution_steps.explain: Find value of first variable, then substitute back to find the second variable.

concepts.title: Elimination Method for Solving Linear Equations
concepts.definition: Solving linear systems by scaling equations to equalize coefficients of one variable and eliminating it through addition or subtraction.
concepts.key_idea: Eliminate a variable by matching its coefficients across equations to simplify solution.
question_patterns: solve the pair of linear equations using elimination method
eliminate one variable to solve the system of linear equations
find the values of x and y by elimination method
apply elimination technique to solve the given pair of equations
use elimination by equating coefficients to solve for variables

solution_steps.action: Multiply equations by suitable constants
solution_steps.explain: Make the numerical coefficients of one selected variable equal in both equations.

solution_steps.action: Add or subtract equations to eliminate one variable
solution_steps.explain: Eliminate the matched variable to get a linear equation in the remaining variable.

solution_steps.action: Solve for the variable and substitute back
solution_steps.explain: Calculate value of the remaining variable and substitute into an original equation to find the other.

concepts.title: Evaluating Slope Parameter in Linear Equation
concepts.definition: Determining the linear parameter or slope m from a given linear equation relationship after determining variable values.
concepts.key_idea: Isolate parameter m using arithmetic operations on coordinates and constant offset.
question_patterns: find the value of m for which y = mx + c
calculate parameter m given values of x and y

evaluate slope m from given coordinates and constant term

solution_steps.action: subtract constant c from y
solution_steps.explain: isolate term m*x

solution_steps.action: divide difference by x
solution_steps.explain: solve for m

solution_steps.action: verify m satisfies the original equation
solution_steps.explain: substitute m back into y = m*x + c to confirm both sides are equal

concepts.title: Calculating Total Cost from Fixed and Variable Rates
concepts.definition: Calculating overall monetary charge composed of a fixed base fee plus a per-unit variable rate multiplied by quantity.
concepts.key_idea: Total expenditure equals fixed fee plus variable rate times usage.
question_patterns: calculate total charge for travelling a given distance

worked_examples.question_pattern: Check graphically whether the pair of equations x + 3y = 6 and 2x - 3y = 12 is consistent. If so, solve them graphically.

solution_template.action: Find solution tables for both linear equations
solution_template.explain: For x + 3y = 6, points are (0,2) and (6,0). For 2x - 3y = 12, points are (0,-4) and (3,-2).

solution_template.action: Plot lines on graph paper and locate intersection
solution_template.explain: The lines intersect at point B(6, 0), so the system is consistent with solution x = 6, y = 0.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Graphically, find whether the pair of equations 5x - 8y + 1 = 0 and 3x - (24/5)y + (3/5) = 0 has no solution, unique solution or infinitely many solutions.

solution_template.explain: Multiplying 3x - (24/5)y + (3/5) = 0 by 5/3 yields 5x - 8y + 1 = 0, which is identical to equation 1.
Since both equations are identical, the lines coincide and have infinitely many solutions.

solution_template.action: Multiply equations to equate coefficients of y
solution_template.explain: Multiply 9x - 4y = 2000 by 3 to get 27x - 12y = 6000. Multiply 7x - 3y = 2000 by 4 to get 28x - 12y = 8000.
